newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to agree nuclear deals in January.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to agree nuclear deals in January.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to agree in January contracts to modernise two nuclear reactors at the Kozloduy plant and to build a storage facility for spent fuel, Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said on Saturday.
Kozloduy meets more than 40 percent of Bulgaria's fuel needs.
The energy ministry issued two tenders earlier this year for the modernisation of two 1,000-megawatt reactors at Kozloduy and for a new fuel storage facility.
"We will announce the winners of the two tenders in January next year," Ovcharov told Reuters.
Kozloduy's reactor number five has been in operation since 1987, while number six was licensed in December 1993 after a two-year commissioning period.
A consortium of Siemens AG, Framatome and a Russian institute is among the bidders. Westinghouse Electric Corp is also in the running.
